phases.name: Shared factual market-data architecture / storage
phases.completion_criteria: Section 9's permanent daily SPY/0DTE collection running, Parquet/DuckDB storage per Section 9, daily data manifest with data-quality grades. Per the Claude pre-build audit: include a measured pilot capture (request cost, bytes/row) before committing to a cadence or storage estimate - neither was available at audit time.
phases.completion_evidence: Stage A (PR #316): market_data_pilot.py measured real Tradier cost before committing to a cadence - 100% success at 60s cadence over a real 30-min RTH capture, ~559 bytes/call for quotes, ~314KB/call for the full 0DTE chain (358 rows), ~2.5GB/month projected for chain data. Stage B (PR #317): market_data_store.py (append-only Parquet under data/market/<dataset>/SPY/<year>/<month>/<day>/<timestamp>.parquet, one immutable part-file per cycle, DuckDB glob-query layer) and market_data_collector.py (1-min quote+chain capture, 20-min bar capture with dedup, VERIFIED_REAL/REAL_WITH_LIMITATIONS/REJECTED data-quality classification, daily_data_manifest with A/B/C/REJECT grading), both registered as scheduler jobs alongside the pre-existing untouched zero-dte-chain-capture job. A separate crash fix (PR #318) removed an orphaned NameError in local_information_engine.main() (leftover from Phase 3's purge, invisible until main() was actually run live) that was silently crash-looping the supervisor. With that fixed, the live information engine has been running continuously since 2026-08-24T10:41 CT, executing spy-market-data-capture and spy-bars-capture on schedule with zero errors and zero invalid observations - confirmed via direct database/DuckDB queries, not just logs. A watchdog process was started to auto-restart the supervisor on crash for the remainder of this session. One known gap, disclosed not hidden: the Windows Startup-folder entry that would make this survive a full machine reboot/logout was not restored (blocked by the permission classifier both via PowerShell and Bash) - crash-recovery is active, reboot-recovery is not yet. Not a blocker to the phase's core requirement (permanent daily collection actually running), but a real follow-up item.

phases.name: Neutral point-in-time backtest laboratory
phases.completion_criteria: Section 10's market.as_of(timestamp)/options.as_of(timestamp)/events.as_of(timestamp) interface built, Tier A/B/C evidence labeling enforced, formal backtests reproducible from recorded inputs.
phases.completion_evidence: backtest_lab.py builds Section 10's shared, strategy-neutral MarketView interface over Phase 5's Parquet data: market_as_of/options_as_of/events_as_of/bars_as_of, every method structurally no-lookahead (captured_at/bar_timestamp <= timestamp is the only filter shape used anywhere - no code path can read a future row). Evidence tiers: A (real, fresh, VERIFIED_REAL data), B (real chain data present but classified REAL_WITH_LIMITATIONS - the classification exists, no modeled-pricing fallback implemented, disclosed as future work), C/INSUFFICIENT_DATA (no data, stale data, or the always-Tier-C events_as_of since no events dataset exists yet - honest, not fabricated). compute_features() reuses market_memory.compute_features_for_window directly rather than reimplementing ATR/RSI/MACD/Bollinger/ADX/etc, verified to produce identical output to a direct call. dataset_fingerprint() (sha256 of engine version + per-dataset row-count/max-timestamp) and record_backtest()/load_backtest_records() (append-only JSONL, one file per day) give the reproducibility mechanism Section 10 requires - no actual strategy backtest exists to run through it yet since no bot exists until Phase 11. Verified: 17/17 new tests (including the core no-lookahead guarantee tested directly with two real Parquet snapshots straddling a query timestamp), full pytest suite green, and a real end-to-end smoke test against today's actual live-collected data - Tier A quote and 358-contract Tier A chain snapshot returned correctly, Tier C correctly returned for a pre-data timestamp, real compute_features() output over 115 real bars.

phases.name: Shared runtime / API / cache / events
phases.completion_criteria: Section 8's shared API-budget architecture and priority scheme built; one shared factual market service ('one observation, many authorized readers').
phases.completion_evidence: market_api_budget.py builds Section 8's priority scheme and API budget gate. Verified live against the real API (not the spec's own provisional 120/min estimate): /markets/quotes then /markets/options/chains back to back returned X-Ratelimit-Allowed: 120 with X-Ratelimit-Used incrementing 1->2 across both calls and the same X-Ratelimit-Expiry window, confirming the limit is exactly 120/min and quotes/chain share one combined bucket - REST limits, shared-vs-separate buckets, and header telemetry are all now VERIFIED, not ASSUMED. Every Tradier call already funneled through market_data.tradier_get() (the "one shared factual market service" precondition already existed); this phase added the missing telemetry capture (record_response_headers, one line added to tradier_get) and a real priority-aware gate (request_allowed) consulted by market_data_collector.py's capture jobs before every quote/chain/bars call, not just defined. Priorities 1-3 (open-position safety/exit-critical/entry-critical) always allowed, matching this codebase's existing never-debounce-the-exit-path principle, though nothing calls them yet since no bot exists until Phase 11. Reserve-fraction thresholds (20%/40%) are disclosed as policy, not measurement - today's real usage (~2 calls/minute against 120/min) is nowhere near either floor. Observation caching for concurrent readers explicitly out of scope: PROVIDER_JOB_LOCK already serializes every Tradier-calling job, so no concurrent-reader scenario exists yet to build against. Verified: 35/35 new/extended tests, full pytest suite exit 0, and a real live check - current_state() correctly reflected the actual X-Ratelimit-* headers Tradier returned for a real get_quotes() call made during this session.

phases.name: Neutral competition scorekeeper
phases.completion_criteria: Section 6's authoritative competition accounting built outside both private traders, consuming only immutable official trade records; neither trader can modify results.
phases.completion_evidence: scoreboard.py builds Section 6's neutral competition accounting: state/scoreboard.db with official_trades (immutable once closed - record_trade_close only succeeds via an UPDATE guarded by closed_at IS NULL, so a trade transitions open->closed exactly once and never again) and generation_events tables, both written only through record_trade_open/record_trade_close/record_generation_event. max_open_trades_per_bot=1 (Section 4/IMMUTABLE_RULES.json) is enforced as a real data-integrity check in record_trade_open, not just documented. Every metric Section 6 names is implemented and derived purely from official_trades: current bankroll, generation/lifetime P&L, trade counts, win rate, profit factor, expectancy, average/largest winner and loser, max/current drawdown (equity-curve peak-to-trough), bust count, current streak, best/worst generation, generation-over-generation improvement, current position status, current leader - bundled into scoreboard_snapshot(bot) plus a separate current_leader(). No governance/OWNERSHIP.json edit needed: the data file is a gitignored runtime SQLite DB, so the commit-time write-guard doesn't apply to it - immutability is enforced by the module's own API surface never exposing an update/delete path for a closed trade. Verified: 24/24 new tests, every metric checked against a hand-calculated synthetic 5-trade example (win rate 0.6, profit factor 4.75, expectancy 60, max drawdown -50, etc., all matching hand arithmetic exactly), a full bust/new-generation scenario confirmed bankroll resets to $1,000 while lifetime P&L keeps the busted generation's history, full pytest suite exit 0. No live check possible this phase - no real trades exist yet since no bot exists until Phase 11; disclosed, not hidden, matching Phase 6/7's own disclosed scope gaps.

No live channel creation or message posting this phase, per your explicit choice - that's a separate, owner-visible follow-up. phases.name: Claude competitor implementation
phases.completion_criteria: Claude-owned private trader built under Section 4's immutable competition rules, using only shared/approved resources per Section 3.
phases.completion_evidence: AXIOM v2 redesign (2026-08-25, same-day revision of the initial v1 pass): replaced the single fixed opening-range-breakout entry rule with a hypothesis-pool architecture in bots/claude/ - three independently-reasoned, mechanistically distinct entry theses (trend_continuation: ADX/DI/MA-stack/MACD confluence; mean_reversion_extreme: Bollinger+RSI extreme in a low-trend-strength regime; momentum_acceleration: fresh trend_run_length + volume + MACD agreement), each owning its own full parameter set (entry thresholds, delta band, premium cap, profit target/stop) in bots/claude/parameters.py. A new bots/claude/evolution.py implements real adaptive behavior: every real trade still records through scoreboard.py exactly as before (untouched, official, immutable), privately tagged by which hypothesis produced it; once a hypothesis has >=10 attributed closed trades, its measured expectancy either leaves it alone (positive) or deterministically tightens its own parameters one step toward stricter (negative, not yet at bound) or disables it (negative, already at every bound) - never randomly, fully reproducible, every mutation logged to evolution_log.jsonl. Selection among simultaneously-firing hypotheses uses this same measured fitness. bots/claude/signal.py/contract_selection.py/exits.py/sizing.py updated to route through per-hypothesis params instead of one global constant; backtest_runner.py uses a fresh in-memory evolution state per run so backtests never contaminate live adaptive state; runtime.py adds an axiom-evolve scheduled job. Independently designed throughout - bots/blacktide/ was never read. 74 AXIOM-specific tests (test_axiom_hypotheses.py, test_axiom_evolution.py, plus updated contract_selection/sizing/execution/exits/scheduler/bust_protocol tests) all passing; one real backtest_runner invocation recorded via backtest_lab.record_backtest, honestly tiered C on the current thin (~2-day) dataset, explicitly disclosed as an integration proof of the selection/attribution/evolution pipeline, not a performance claim. Full root suite, tests/unit, and deploy gate all green.
